statements.impact_statement: Measured 2026-11-19 on the gitlab-foss v19.6.0 source. The advisory covers Lockbox's hybrid algorithm (public/private key pair), where holding the encryption key is enough to decrypt. GitLab uses Lockbox only through its CarrierWave integration with a symmetric key and the default algorithm: app/uploaders/ci/secure_file_uploader.rb:10 encrypt(key: :key), app/uploaders/ci/pipeline_artifact_uploader.rb:11 and app/uploaders/terraform/state_uploader.rb:13 encrypt(key: ..., previous_versions: ...), with keys derived by HMAC-SHA256 from db_key_base (lib/gitlab/encryption/db_key_base_lockbox_keys.rb). No file in app/, lib/, config/, gems/ or vendor/gems/ selects algorithm hybrid or generates a key pair. The fix is only in lockbox 2.3.0, a new major; GitLab master still locks 1.4.1. Revisit when GitLab moves to lockbox 2.x or adds hybrid encryption.

Measured 2026-11-19 on the gitlab-foss v19.6.0 source and rubyzip v2.4.1. The flaw is the destination check in the 3.x extraction path, which compares the entry's expanded path with the destination directory by prefix without a trailing separator; in 2.4.1 that check lives only in Entry#extract_v3 (lib/zip/entry.rb:213-217) and File#extract_v3 (lib/zip/file.rb:387-391). GitLab never calls them: no extract_v3 or destination_directory in app/, lib/, config/, gems/ or vendor/gems/. Its two extraction sites pass an explicit destination to the 2.x API, File#extract -> Entry#extract(dest_path) (lib/zip/file.rb:374-379, lib/zip/entry.rb:191-206): SafeZip (gems/safe_zip/lib/safe_zip/entry.rb:11 computes the path, :55 extracts) only extracts paths that match a target file exactly or a target directory joined with a trailing separator (gems/safe_zip/lib/safe_zip/extract_params.rb:15-23, 38-41), and refuses symlinks and parent directories that resolve elsewhere (entry.rb:62-82); NuGet symbol extraction writes one entry to a temp file path it created (app/services/packages/nuget/symbols/create_symbol_files_service.rb:33). The fix is only in rubyzip 3.4.0, a new major whose extract API differs; GitLab master still locks 2.4.1. Revisit when GitLab moves to rubyzip 3.x or calls extract_v3.

Measured 2026-11-19 on gitlab-foss v19.6.0. GitLab enables Confirmable with email changes (app/models/user.rb:132-133), so the race in postpone_email_change_until_confirmation_and_regenerate_confirmation_token is reachable on an unpatched gem. The fix forces unconfirmed_email into every update (lib/devise/models/confirmable.rb and lib/devise/orm.rb, devise commit 02527772bd). The image builds GitLab's locked devise 4.9.4 (the fixes ship only in the 5.0 line, a major that changes Rails and Ruby support; GitLab master still locks 4.9.4) and applies the upstream library diffs of devise commits 02527772bd (v5.0.3) and 025fe2124f (v5.0.4) as apps/gitlab-rails/devise-4.9.4-security.patch right after bundle install; the build fails unless both fix lines are present in the installed gem (apps/gitlab-rails/melange.yaml, the devise step). The installed gem still reports version 4.9.4, which is why scanners flag it. Revisit when GitLab moves to devise 5.

Measured 2026-11-19 on gitlab-foss v19.6.0. GitLab does not enable Timeoutable, but its session enforcer throws the same :timeout failure (lib/gitlab/auth/session_expire_from_init_enforcer.rb:61) and its failure app inherits Devise::FailureApp#redirect_url (lib/gitlab/devise_failure.rb:4), so the unvalidated non-GET request.referrer redirect is reachable on an unpatched gem. The fix passes the referrer through extract_path_from_location (lib/devise/failure_app.rb and lib/devise/controllers/store_location.rb, devise commit 025fe2124f). The image builds GitLab's locked devise 4.9.4 (the fixes ship only in the 5.0 line, a major that changes Rails and Ruby support; GitLab master still locks 4.9.4) and applies the upstream library diffs of devise commits 02527772bd (v5.0.3) and 025fe2124f (v5.0.4) as apps/gitlab-rails/devise-4.9.4-security.patch right after bundle install; the build fails unless both fix lines are present in the installed gem (apps/gitlab-rails/melange.yaml, the devise step). The installed gem still reports version 4.9.4, which is why scanners flag it. Revisit when GitLab moves to devise 5.

Measured 2026-11-19 on gitlab-foss v19.6.0 and rack-proxy v0.8.3. The flaw is in Rack::Proxy forwarding a backend response: it drops Transfer-Encoding and keeps the backend's Content-Length (lib/rack/proxy.rb:181 in 0.8.3 has the same pattern as the 1.0.x releases the advisory names). GitLab mounts a Rack::Proxy only in development: Gitlab::Middleware::IamServiceProxy is added only if Rails.env.development? (config/initializers/iam_service_proxy.rb:8-10) and Gitlab::Webpack::DevServerMiddleware only if the webpack dev server is enabled in a dev or test environment (config/initializers/static_files.rb:20-27). The image runs RAILS_ENV=production (apps/gitlab-rails/apko.yaml). The one other use, Rack::Proxy.extract_http_request_headers in lib/gitlab/current/organization.rb:15, reads request headers and proxies nothing. The fix is only in rack-proxy 1.0.3, a new major GitLab pins away from (Gemfile:402 ~> 0.8.0; master still locks 0.8.3). Revisit if GitLab proxies through Rack::Proxy in production.

Measured 2026-11-19 on gitlab-foss v19.6.0 and carrierwave v1.3.4. The flaw is in carrierwave's own Content-Type allowlist: CarrierWave::Uploader::ContentTypeWhitelist#check_content_type_whitelist! checks the client-supplied content type with a partial match in whitelisted_content_type? (lib/carrierwave/uploader/content_type_whitelist.rb:35-43 in 1.3.4). GitLab replaces both methods: ContentTypeWhitelist::Concern (app/uploaders/content_type_whitelist.rb:28-41) is included in GitlabUploader (app/uploaders/gitlab_uploader.rb:4), the only class in app/, lib/ and gems/ that subclasses CarrierWave::Uploader::Base (gitlab_uploader.rb:3), so it overrides carrierwave's methods for every uploader; GitLab's check runs on the type detected from the file's magic bytes (Gitlab::Utils::MimeType.from_io, content_type_whitelist.rb:43-50), not a type the client sends. The only uploaders that set an allowlist inherit it: AvatarUploader < GitlabUploader (avatar_uploader.rb:3) and FaviconUploader < AttachmentUploader < GitlabUploader (favicon_uploader.rb:3, attachment_uploader.rb:3). The fixes are only in carrierwave 2.2.x / 3.x; GitLab 19.6 and master lock 1.3.4 (its uploaders are written against 1.x), and css_parser 3.x cannot be resolved alongside it (ssrf_filter caps). Revisit when GitLab moves to carrierwave 2 or drops ContentTypeWhitelist::Concern.

Measured 2026-11-19 on gitlab-foss v19.6.0 and carrierwave v1.3.4. The flaw is carrierwave's content-type denylist not escaping regex metacharacters. GitLab never sets a content-type denylist: no content_type_denylist or content_type_blacklist in app/, lib/, config/, gems/ or vendor/gems/ (the only match is an error-message string in config/locales/carrierwave.en.yml); its uploaders use allowlists, which GitLab implements itself (app/uploaders/content_type_whitelist.rb). The fixes are only in carrierwave 2.2.x / 3.x; GitLab 19.6 and master lock 1.3.4 (its uploaders are written against 1.x), and css_parser 3.x cannot be resolved alongside it (ssrf_filter caps). Revisit when GitLab moves to carrierwave 2 or drops ContentTypeWhitelist::Concern.

The flaw is SSRF and local-file disclosure in CssParser::Parser#read_remote_file, reached through load_uri! or an @import inside parsed CSS; no CSS that css_parser parses here is attacker-controlled, and premailer-rails removes the links premailer would fetch. Measured 2026-11-19 on gitlab-foss v19.6.0, premailer 1.27.0, premailer-rails 1.12.0 and css_parser 1.22.0. In the CE image css_parser is reached only through premailer, which inlines CSS into outgoing mail (config/initializers/action_mailer_hooks.rb:18, app/workers/emails_on_push_worker.rb:112). premailer-rails strips every <link rel=stylesheet> from the mail (premailer-rails lib/premailer/rails/css_helper.rb:26-33) and hands premailer the CSS as a string from the asset pipeline only, the production strategy (config/initializers/premailer.rb:10; customized_premailer.rb:14), so premailer's load_uri! path never runs; css_parser parses that GitLab-built asset CSS and the <style> blocks of the mail HTML (premailer lib/premailer/premailer.rb:282-283, 330-331). Mail HTML comes from GitLab's own templates plus user markdown rendered through Banzai's sanitizer, whose element allowlist has no style element (html-pipeline 2.14.3 lib/html/pipeline/sanitization_filter.rb:43-50; GitLab adds only span, details, summary, abbr, section and input: gems/gitlab-banzai/lib/banzai/filter/base_sanitization_filter.rb:30-46, lib/banzai/filter/sanitization_filter.rb:85-95) and which reduces style attributes to text-align on table cells (lib/banzai/filter/sanitization_filter.rb:36-38, 107-112). The other dependents do not run in the CE image: prawn-svg backs only lib/gitlab/pdf, which nothing in the foss tree calls (its callers are in ee/), and lookbook is in the development group (Gemfile:534). The fixes are only in css_parser 3.x, which needs ssrf_filter ~> 1.5 while carrierwave 1.3.4 caps it below 1.1 and GitLab's config/initializers/ssrf_filter_patch.rb:8 refuses ssrf_filter >= 1.2, so the bundle cannot resolve; GitLab master still locks 1.22.0. Revisit when GitLab moves to carrierwave 2 and css_parser 3, or lets user content carry <style>.

The flaw is an arbitrary local-file read through an attacker-controlled @import in parsed CSS; the CSS css_parser parses here is GitLab's own asset and template CSS, and user markdown cannot add a <style> element. The flaw is a ReDoS in RuleSet#expand_shorthand! on crafted dimension shorthands (margin/padding values with unclosed functions); user-controlled style attributes are reduced to text-align: left, center or right before premailer sees them, and the stylesheets are GitLab's own. Measured 2026-11-19 on the image's compiled frontend. The match is a name collision: the file is srv/gitlab/public/assets/webpack/gitlab-web-ide-vscode-workbench-0.0.1-dev-20260106142046/vscode/extensions/diff/package.json, the manifest of a VS Code built-in language extension that GitLab's Web IDE ships (npm @gitlab/web-ide 0.0.1-dev-20260106142046, package/.../vscode/extensions/diff/package.json: name diff, version 1.0.0, publisher vscode, engines.vscode set), not the npm package of that name. The npm package diff is not in the image: the frontend is compiled into public/assets and node_modules is removed at build (apps/gitlab-rails/melange.yaml, install step). The Web IDE reads these manifests at runtime, so they stay.
